topic: Clicking or clunking hip: when it matters

slides.headline: Hip clunks when you move?
slides.sub: Most clicks are harmless noise. Here's how to tell when it matters.

slides.title: Noise alone is usually fine
slides.body: Plenty of hips click or clunk during leg raises, squats or getting out of the car. If it doesn't hurt and you can move normally, it's usually just a tendon sliding over bone.

slides.title: Common harmless culprits
slides.body: A band of tissue flicking over the bony point on the side of the hip, or the hip flexor tendon at the front, are frequent sources. Dancers and gym-goers notice these a lot.

slides.title: Clicking plus pain is different
slides.body: Clicking with a deep, catching pain in the groin, a sense of the hip locking or giving way, or pain that builds with sitting can point to a joint issue that's worth assessing.

slides.title: What usually helps
slides.body: Strengthening the glutes, hip flexors and trunk, and adjusting the movements that provoke it, can often reduce painful clicking. Chasing the noise with stretching alone rarely changes much.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A hip that locks, pain that stops you walking normally, pain after a fall, or groin pain with fever deserve a prompt assessment rather than more stretching.

caption:
Does your hip clunk every time you lift your leg? In most cases, that noise is harmless.

Hips often click as tendons slide over bony points, especially in dancers, runners and gym-goers. If there's no pain and you move normally, it usually needs nothing at all.

It's a different story when the click comes with deep groin pain, catching, locking or a feeling the hip might give way. That combination is worth getting assessed, and strengthening the muscles around the hip is often part of the plan.
